provenance.notes: Unlike HRRR's/GFS's/NBM's manifests, this pilot's production code (data/gefs.py, scripts/pilot_phase6_gefs.py including its launch driver) was fully committed at commit 35f0d69 BEFORE extraction began -- no uncommitted fixes were required during or after the run. The entire 62,744-item dataset is reproducible from this single commit. Production output used its own dedicated directory (data/processed/pilot/gefs/), never shared with any validation/benchmark script (all prior GEFS investigation work ran from Claude's scratchpad directory, outside the repo) -- confirmed via a pre-launch check that the directory did not yet exist, and post-run reconciliation confirming the checkpoint's 62,744 keys match the independently-recomputed canonical work-item set exactly (0 missing, 0 extra), unlike the NBM pilot's earlier cross-contamination incident. 203 of the 62,744 items failed on the first pass with transient network errors (ConnectionReset/RemoteDisconnected/IncompleteRead, clustered mostly around one burst near 2025-01-21T18:00Z across many members/FHs, consistent with a brief S3-side blip); all 203 were retried successfully using the unmodified production extraction path with 0 further failures.

source.name: gefs
source.fh0_semantics: TMP/DPT/RH/UGRD/VGRD/PRES present and meaningful at F0 (forecast_desc='anl'). APCP/TCDC/DSWRF structurally absent at F0 (0 idx entries, not a selection ambiguity). TMAX/TMIN at F0 use a degenerate zero-width '0-0 day max/min fcst' window (lengthOfTimeRange=0) -- explicitly skipped in production code, confirmed 0 rows for these 5 variables at forecast_hour=0 in the final dataset.
source.window_semantics: APCP/TCDC/DSWRF/TMAX/TMIN share one accumulation/average/period window convention: cumulative-since-start for FH<=6, then resets every 6h synoptic mark for FH>6 (window_start=6*floor((FH-1)/6)). No duplicate products exist for any variable at any forecast hour (unlike HRRR/GFS/NBM's APCP) -- find_message()'s exact-match lookup is safe. Window is always parsed from the observed forecast_desc text via data.gefs.parse_forecast_desc(), never computed from the formula.
source.completeness_rule: Conservative complete-ensemble rule (data/weather_state.py::assess_ensemble_run_completeness, unchanged from an earlier architecture phase, independently re-validated in this phase): a run is usable_for_daily_max only when all 31 expected members have all expected target-day valid times present.

runtime_overrides.note: matches scripts/pilot_phase6_gefs.py's own committed default (independently benchmarked for GEFS, see docs/gefs_pilot_readiness.md sections 15-16) -- no override needed

performance.estimate_vs_actual_note: Pre-launch estimates (docs/gefs_pilot_readiness.md sections 17-18, from a 20-item benchmark sample) were ~396 GB remote / ~65 MB local / ~6.0h runtime. Actual full-scale production run: ~402.8 GB remote (close match), ~51.1 MB local (lower than estimated -- the benchmark's rows/item blend overestimated F0-vs-non-F0 item mix slightly), ~4.64h runtime (faster than estimated, same pattern observed in the HRRR/GFS/NBM pilots -- a sustained long run's steady-state throughput exceeds short repeated-trial benchmark throughput).
